mainTopic: Whether the worry about a woman's expected period (וסתות) is דאורייתא or דרבנן, and how often she must check herself
overview: This amud opens by finishing a discussion about a כהן who looked into a pit where a maidservant had thrown a miscarried fetus. The גמרא gives two reasons why he stays טהור without breaking the rule that a doubt cannot override a certainty. First, the object itself may not have been a נפל. Second, the animals there surely dragged it away. Then the חכמים ask רב נחמן whether the worry about a woman's expected period (וסתות) is דאורייתא or דרבנן, and he answers both ways from a ruling of רב. Next comes a מחלוקת between רב and שמואל about a woman who missed her check and checked later. רבי זירא and רב נחמן בר יצחק differ on whether that argument is really about וסתות. רב ששת and אביי find the same dispute among תנאים. רבינא, though, shows that a ברייתא about blood from a wound is really about whether the מקור makes blood טמא. The amud ends with a new משנה: בית שמאי require two checking cloths for every act of תשמיש, while בית הלל say two cloths are enough for the whole night.

steps.title: She threw something that only looked like a fetus
steps.stepSummary: This line ends the גמרא's answer: the maidservant threw something 'like a נפל', so it was never certain that there was טומאה in the pit.
steps.simpleTranslation: [She threw] something like a stillborn fetus.
steps.whatsHappening: These two words finish the גמרא's answer from the line before. The ברייתא's case is that she threw an object that only looked like a נפל, so we are not sure there was any טומאה at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was how the כהן could stay טהור when there was a certain טומאה and only a doubt that animals removed it. If the object itself is in doubt (maybe it was just a lump of blood), we now have one doubt on top of another, a ספק ספיקא. So the rule that a ספק cannot override a ודאי no longer applies.

keyTerms.meaning: A miscarried or non-viable fetus, which can carry טומאת מת
A doubt cannot override a certainty
A double doubt, where each doubt leans toward leniency

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. These two words are the end of an answer that started before this section, so read them as the final part of that sentence.

phrases.english: Something like a stillborn fetus.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun just before this section, to the question of a ספק overriding a ודאי.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There was a definite נפל in the pit, so only the dragging away was in doubt.
steps.terutzMaskana: The object itself was in doubt, so the case is a doubt against a doubt.

steps.title: But the ברייתא says he looked to see if it was male or female
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: the ברייתא's wording shows the only question was the baby's gender, so it was definitely a נפל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא teaches that he looked 'to know if it was male or female'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave by pointing to the exact words of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the כהן only wanted to know whether it was male or female, then everyone took for granted that it really was a נפל. That brings back the original problem: a certain טומאה against only a doubt that animals removed it.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא ״לֵידַע אִם זָכָר אִם נְקֵבָה״ קָתָנֵי!
phrases.english: But it teaches 'to know whether male or whether female'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא לֵידַע אִם זָכָר אִם נְקֵבָה קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 1 using the ברייתא's wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the object was only 'like a נפל'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא describes asking only about gender, which assumes a definite נפל.

steps.title: Rereading the ברייתא: first whether it was a fetus, then male or female
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא means the כהן looked first to see whether it was a נפל or just a shapeless mass, and only after that whether it was male or female.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: the כהן came and looked to know whether she miscarried a fetus or just a shapeless mass. And if you say it was a fetus, then he wanted to know whether it was male or female.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends its answer by explaining that the ברייתא leaves out a step. The 'male or female' question came only after a first question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first question was whether this was a real נפל at all. 'Male or female' is only a follow-up question, in case it turned out to be a נפל. So the wording does not prove it was definitely a נפל, and the double-doubt answer still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (introducing a rereading)
Literally 'wind'; here a shapeless mass with no real fetus
And if you say (that the first possibility is true)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא hides a two-level question: first, was it a fetus at all? Then, if so, male or female? So the case stays a doubt against a doubt.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
And a priest came and peered at it,
to know whether she miscarried a fetus
or whether she miscarried 'wind',
phrases.notes: 'Wind' means something with no real form, not an actual baby.

phrases.english: and if you say she miscarried a fetus,
[then] to know whether male or whether female.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2 by reading the ברייתא as a question with two levels.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Male or female' shows it was certainly a נפל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The gender question was secondary, asked only if it was a נפל, so the main doubt remains.

steps.title: Second answer: the animals certainly dragged it away
steps.stepSummary: Another answer: since weasels and hyenas are common there, they surely dragged the fetus away, so this is a certainty against a certainty.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say this: since weasels and hyenas are common there, they certainly dragged it away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different way to answer the original problem. It accepts that it may have been a real נפל and changes the doubt about the animals into a certainty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer turned the case into a doubt against a doubt. This answer works the other way: because these animals are found there so often, it is treated as certain that they removed the fetus. That gives a certainty against a certainty, so a doubt never overrides a certainty here.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (introducing an alternative answer)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to how the כהן stayed טהור: (1) it was a doubt against a doubt, since the object may not have been a נפל; or (2) it was a certainty against a certainty, since the animals surely took it.
steps.whyThisMatters: Both answers protect the rule that a ספק cannot override a ודאי. They explain why this case does not break that rule.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
since weasels and hyenas are common there,
they certainly dragged it away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the original question, instead of the 'like a נפל' answer of steps 1-3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Raising the doubt to a certainty (ודאי against ודאי)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The animals only possibly removed it, which would be a doubt against a certainty.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the animals are so common there, the removal counts as certain, so a certainty stands against a certainty.

steps.title: Are expected periods a Torah law or a rabbinic law?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask רב נחמן whether the worry about a woman's expected period comes from the Torah or from the Rabbis.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked רב נחמן: are וסתות from the Torah or from the Rabbis?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. It asks how strong the law of וסתות is: Torah level or rabbinic level.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If וסתות are דאורייתא, a woman who did not check at her expected time is assumed to have had a period without noticing, so she is טמאה. If they are only דרבנן, she can still check later and be טהורה.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman's fixed, expected times for her period

phrases.english: They asked Rav Nachman:
Are expected periods from the Torah or from the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, separate from the case about the maidservant and the נפל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the law of וסתות is דאורייתא or דרבנן.

steps.title: רב נחמן proves from רב's ruling that expected periods are Torah law
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן cites רב: a woman who did not check at her expected time and later saw blood is worried about both times, so וסתות are דאורייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: from what הונא our colleague said in the name of רב: a woman with a fixed cycle whose expected time came, who did not check, and later saw blood, worries about her expected time and also worries about her seeing. This shows that וסתות are from the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the question with a ruling of רב. Because the ruling is strict, he concludes that וסתות are דאורייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב makes her טמאה going back to her expected time, and not only from when she found blood. That strictness only makes sense if her expected time has Torah force.

keyTerms.meaning: She must be concerned, so she treats herself as possibly טמאה

phrases.english: He said to them:
From what Huna our colleague said in the name of Rav:
A woman who has a fixed cycle,
and the time of her period arrived and she did not check,
and in the end she saw blood:
she is concerned from the time of her period,
phrases.notes: Anything טהור that she touched since her expected time becomes טמא.

phrases.english: and she is concerned for her seeing.
phrases.notes: This means the 24 hours before she found the blood.

phrases.english: Evidently, expected periods are from the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ מִדְּאָמַר הוּנָא חַבְרִין מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: וסתות are דאורייתא, because רב treats her strictly from the time of her expected period.

steps.title: Another version: the same ruling shows expected periods are rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: Some report that רב נחמן read רב's ruling the other way: she is only טמאה because she saw blood, so וסתות are דרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say this is what he told them: the reason she is טמאה is that she saw blood. But if she did not see blood, we are not concerned. This shows that וסתות are from the Rabbis.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רב נחמן's answer. It uses the same ruling of רב but reaches the opposite conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the focus is on the words 'in the end she saw.' רב was only strict because blood was found. If she checked later and found nothing, we would not worry, even though she skipped checking at her expected time. So וסתות must be only דרבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: But, implied from this: introduces an inference from the opposite case

steps.confusionAlert: Both versions use the exact same ruling of רב. They only disagree about which part of it is the key point: the strictness, or the fact that she saw blood.

phrases.english: There are those who say
this is what he said to them:
The reason is that she saw blood;
but if she did not see blood, we are not concerned.
Evidently, expected periods are from the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second version of step 6 that reaches the opposite answer from the same source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: וסתות are דרבנן, because without seeing blood there is no concern.
steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא leaves both versions standing. Steps 10-12 come back to this question through the argument between רב and שמואל.

steps.title: רב: if she checks later, the later check decides
steps.stepSummary: About a woman who skipped checking at her expected time and checked later, רב rules that whatever the later check shows is her status.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: a woman with a fixed cycle whose expected time came, who did not check, and checked later. רב says: if she checked and found herself טמאה, she is טמאה. If she found herself טהורה, she is טהורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related מחלוקת between רב and שמואל. This step gives רב's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, missing the check at her expected time does not make her טמאה by itself. A later clean check is enough to keep her טהורה. The next steps ask whether this means רב holds וסתות are דרבנן. רבי זירא will say no, and רב נחמן בר יצחק will say yes.

keyTerms.meaning: And in the end, at a later time

phrases.english: It was stated:
A woman who has a fixed cycle,
and the time of her period arrived and she did not check,
and in the end she checked:
Rav says:
if she checked and found herself impure, she is impure;
if she found herself pure, she is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a separate מחלוקת, connected to the ruling of רב quoted in steps 6 and 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A late check decides her status: if clean, she is טהורה.

steps.title: שמואל: even a clean later check leaves her impure
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules she is טמאה even if her later check is clean, because a period comes at its usual time.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל says: even if she checked and found herself טהורה, she is still טמאה, because a woman's period comes at its usual time.
steps.whatsHappening: This is שמואל's side of the מחלוקת. He disagrees with רב and is strict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל assumes that her period surely came at its expected time, even if she did not notice it. So a clean check later cannot undo that. The next step asks whether this is because he holds וסתות are דאורייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'the way': here it means a woman's period

steps.whatToRemember: רב: a later clean check makes her טהורה. שמואל: she is טמאה anyway, because a period comes at its expected time.

phrases.english: And Shmuel says:
Even if she checked and found herself pure,
she is also impure,
because the way of women comes at its time.
phrases.notes: 'The way of women' is a gentle way of saying her period.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ בָּדְקָה וּמָצָאת טְהוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposing side of the מחלוקת begun in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: She is טמאה even after a clean later check, because a period is assumed to come at its expected time.

steps.title: Do רב and שמואל disagree about whether וסתות are from the Torah?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב and שמואל are really arguing about whether the worry about a woman's expected period is דאורייתא or דרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say they disagree about וסתות: one Sage holds they are from the Torah, and one Sage holds they are from the Rabbis?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to explain the argument between רב and שמואל by tying it to a bigger question: is the worry about an expected period from the Torah or from the Rabbis? This is a suggestion that the next steps will test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל, who says she is טמאה even if her later check is clean, would hold וסתות are דאורייתא. That means missing the check at the expected time is serious. רב, who goes by whatever the later check shows, would hold they are only דרבנן, so a clean later check is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say. The גמרא is proposing an explanation that it may later reject.
A woman's expected times for her period

phrases.english: Shall we say that they disagree about expected periods,
phrases.notes: "They" means רב and שמואל from the last two steps.

phrases.english: that one Sage holds they are from the Torah,
phrases.notes: This is שמואל, who says she is טמאה even if the later check is clean.

phrases.english: and one Sage holds they are from the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: This is רב, who goes by whatever the later check shows.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to link the רב/שמואל argument in steps 8-9 to the question in step 5 about whether וסתות are דאורייתא or דרבנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the argument between רב and שמואל come from a disagreement over whether וסתות are דאורייתא or דרבנן?

steps.title: Everyone agrees וסתות are from the Torah, but the cases are different
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא rejects the suggestion. Everyone holds וסתות are דאורייתא. רב's case is where she checked close to her expected time, and שמואל's case is where she did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: Everyone agrees וסתות are from the Torah. Here, she checked herself within the time of a period. There, she did not check herself within the time of a period.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא says we do not need to tie רב and שמואל to the big question. They agree on it, and each is talking about a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she checked close enough to her expected time, a clean check shows nothing came at the expected time, so רב says she is טהורה. If she checked later than that, the clean check does not prove anything about the expected time, so שמואל says she is טמאה. The argument becomes a difference in cases, not in principle.

keyTerms.meaning: Here... there. Used to show that two rulings are about two different cases.
Within the length of time a period takes to come, meaning close to the expected time

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read רבי זירא as saying רב and שמואל disagree. In his view they simply rule on two different cases, and both hold וסתות are דאורייתא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
Everyone agrees that expected periods are from the Torah,
here, it is where she checked herself within the time of a period,
phrases.notes: This is רב's case, so her clean check counts and she is טהורה.

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן — שֶׁלֹּא בָּדְקָה עַצְמָהּ כְּשִׁיעוּר וֶסֶת.
phrases.english: there, it is where she did not check herself within the time of a period.
phrases.notes: This is שמואל's case, so the later clean check does not help her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא וְסָתוֹת דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the לימא in step 10 by splitting the cases.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that רב and שמואל disagree about whether וסתות are דאורייתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The suggestion assumed both rulings are about the same case. In fact they differ in how close to her expected time she checked.

steps.title: They really do disagree about וסתות themselves
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק disagrees with רבי זירא and says that רב and שמואל really are arguing about whether וסתות are דאורייתא or דרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: They disagree about וסתות themselves. One Sage holds וסתות are from the Torah, and one Sage holds וסתות are from the Rabbis.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different view: the original suggestion was right after all. רב and שמואל disagree about the basic status of וסתות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word גופייהו ("themselves") stresses that the argument is about the root question, not about a detail of the case like רבי זירא said. So for שמואל they are דאורייתא and she is טמאה, and for רב they are דרבנן and the later clean check is enough.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
They disagree about expected periods themselves,
that one Sage holds: expected periods are from the Torah,
and one Sage holds: expected periods are from the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: בִּוְסָתוֹת גּוּפַיְיהוּ קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי זירא in step 11 and goes back to the suggestion in step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. רב and שמואל disagree about whether וסתות are דאורייתא (שמואל) or דרבנן (רב).

steps.title: The same argument exists among the תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says the רב/שמואל argument matches an earlier argument among תנאים. He begins with רבי אליעזר, who says a woman who did not check at her expected time is טמאה נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: This is like an argument of תנאים. רבי אליעזר says: She is טמאה as a נדה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת starts showing that רב and שמואל are following an older argument among the תנאים. This opens a quoted ברייתא, and the other opinions come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר calls her a real נדה just for missing her check. That treats the expected time as a Torah-level concern, which matches שמואל. The other תנאים, who will be quoted next, will line up with רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the תנאים. This argument already exists among the Sages of the משנה.
Fully טמאה with the status of a נדה

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: It is like an argument of the Tannaim,
Rabbi Eliezer says: She is impure as a menstruating woman.
phrases.notes: This is about a woman who did not check at her expected time. רבי אליעזר's view matches שמואל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the view that רב and שמואל disagree about the status of וסתות by finding the same argument among תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: That the argument between רב and שמואל is an older argument among the תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that opens with רבי אליעזר's view that she is טמאה נדה.

steps.title: רבי יהושע says she should be checked
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע disagrees with רבי אליעזר: a woman who did not check at her expected time can check now, and she is not automatically טמאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע says: she should be checked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the תנאים argument that רב ששת started. רבי יהושע says she can be checked now instead of being treated as טמאה right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר treated her as טמאה נדה because he holds the expected period is a Torah-level worry. רבי יהושע lets a later check decide, which fits the view that וסתות are only דרבנן. So רבי אליעזר matches שמואל, and רבי יהושע matches רב.

keyTerms.meaning: She should be checked (examine herself now)
A self-examination to see whether she has bled

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua says: she should be examined.
phrases.notes: He means she checks now, even though her expected time has already passed. If she is clean, she is טהורה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the תנאים argument that רב ששת began quoting in step 13
steps.raayaObject: That רב and שמואל argue about whether וסתות are דאורייתא or דרבנן
steps.raayaSupportSource: The argument between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע

steps.title: רבי מאיר and the Sages argue the same way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds that the same argument shows up between רבי מאיר, who says טמאה נדה, and חכמים, who say she should be checked.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these תנאים are like those תנאים, as a ברייתא teaches: רבי מאיר says she is טמאה נדה, and חכמים say she should be checked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to a second pair of תנאים who argue exactly like רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר is on the same side as רבי אליעזר: she is טמאה, so וסתות are דאורייתא. חכמים are on the same side as רבי יהושע: she can be checked, so וסתות are דרבנן. This makes the dispute broader than one pair of תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: These תנאים argue the same way as those תנאים
She is impure as a נדה
The Sages, meaning the majority opinion

phrases.english: And these tanna'im are like those tanna'im,
phrases.notes: "These" is רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע; "those" is רבי מאיר and חכמים, who come next.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: טְמֵאָה נִדָּה,
phrases.english: as it is taught: Rabbi Meir says: she is impure as a menstruating woman,
and the Rabbis say: she should be examined.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי תַנָּאֵי כִּי הָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a matching pair of תנאים to the dispute brought in steps 13-14
steps.raayaObject: That the question of whether וסתות are דאורייתא is an old argument among תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with רבי מאיר against חכמים

steps.title: אביי brings a משנה about רבי מאיר and a woman in hiding
steps.stepSummary: אביי says a משנה also shows רבי מאיר's view: a woman hiding in fear who did not check at her expected time is טהורה, because fear stops the bleeding.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We also learn this in a משנה. רבי מאיר says: if she was in hiding, her expected time came, and she did not check, she is טהורה, because fear holds back the blood.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a משנה to back up the claim that רבי מאיר holds וסתות are דאורייתא. Here he quotes the משנה; in the next step he draws the inference from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי מאיר calls the woman טהורה only because she was hiding from danger. Fear is a reason to assume she did not bleed. This prepares a precise inference about the normal case, where there is no fear.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned this, in a משנה
A hiding place, hiding from danger
The time of her expected period
Holds back or stops the blood

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא,
phrases.english: Abaye said: We, too, have learned this,
phrases.notes: He means it is not only in a ברייתא. A משנה also shows רבי מאיר's view.

phrases.english: as we learned in a mishna: Rabbi Meir says:
If she was in hiding,
and the time of her period arrived and she did not examine herself,
she is pure, because fear holds back the blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 15's claim about רבי מאיר with a משנה
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר holds וסתות are דאורייתא
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a woman hiding in fear

steps.title: Without fear she would be impure, so וסתות are Torah law
steps.stepSummary: אביי reasons that only fear made her טהורה. Without fear she would be טמאה, so רבי מאיר holds וסתות are דאורייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason is that there is fear. But if there is no fear, she is טמאה. This shows that וסתות are דאורייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי draws the inference from the משנה he just quoted and finishes his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If fear is the only thing that saves her, then a normal woman who did not check at her expected time would be טמאה. Treating her as definitely טמאה, without letting a later check help, only makes sense if the expected period is a Torah-level matter. So רבי מאיר holds וסתות are דאורייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: The worry about expected periods is Torah law

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר, רבי מאיר and שמואל are on one side: וסתות are דאורייתא. רבי יהושע, חכמים and רב are on the other side: וסתות are דרבנן, so she may check.

phrases.english: The reason she is pure is that there is fear;
but if there is no fear, she is impure.
This shows that the worry about expected periods is Torah law.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּאִיכָּא חֲרָדָה, הָא לֵיכָּא חֲרָדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the משנה quoted in step 16
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר holds וסתות are דאורייתא
steps.raayaSupportSource: An inference from the reason given in the משנה (fear)
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי מאיר holds וסתות are דאורייתא

steps.title: Do רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי also argue about this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether another pair of תנאים argue about the same question. It quotes their ברייתא about a woman who sees blood because of a wound.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say these תנאים also argue about this? A ברייתא teaches: a woman who sees blood because of a wound is טהורה even during her days of נדה; these are the words of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. רבי says: if she has a וסת, she must worry about her וסת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a new pair of תנאים who may be arguing about whether וסתות are דאורייתא, and quotes their ברייתא. This sets up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל blames the blood on the wound, even at her expected time. רבי says that if she has a set וסת, she must worry the blood is from her period. The גמרא wonders whether רבי's worry comes from holding וסתות are דאורייתא. Step 19 spells out this suggestion, and step 20 answers it.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? It opens a suggestion that may be rejected
Her days of נדה, the time she would usually get her period
She must worry about her expected period

steps.confusionAlert: Here "רבי" with no name after it means רבי יהודה הנשיא, not just any rabbi.

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא הָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי בְּהָא נָמֵי פְּלִיגִי,
phrases.english: Shall we say these tanna'im also argue about this matter?
phrases.notes: "This matter" is whether וסתות are דאורייתא or דרבנן.

phrases.english: As it is taught: a woman who sees blood because of a wound,
even during her days of menstruation, is pure;
these are the words of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: אִם יֵשׁ לָהּ וֶסֶת —
phrases.english: Rabbi says: If she has a fixed cycle,
she must be concerned about her period.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא הָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי בְּהָא נָמֵי פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After proving one argument among תנאים, the גמרא checks whether another pair argues the same way
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי argue about whether וסתות are דאורייתא or דרבנן

steps.title: Suggesting the argument is about whether וסתות are Torah law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל argue about whether וסתות are דאורייתא or דרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this what they argue about? One holds וסתות are from the Torah, and the other holds וסתות are from the Rabbis.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the question it started in step 18. It suggests that the two תנאים in the wound ברייתא are arguing about the same question as before: are וסתות דאורייתא or דרבנן?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי is stricter about a woman with a set pattern, so the גמרא suggests he holds וסתות are דאורייתא. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is lenient, so he would hold וסתות are דרבנן. If this is right, we have one more pair of תנאים who argue about this question.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it true that... (opens a suggested proof)
a woman's expected times of seeing blood

phrases.english: Is it not that they argue about this:
that one master holds וסתות are from the Torah,
phrases.notes: "One master" here is רבי, the one who is stricter in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: and the other master holds וסתות are from the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the question from step 18 by saying what the תנאים in the ברייתא might be arguing about.
steps.raayaObject: That the question of וסתות being דאורייתא or דרבנן is also argued by רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about a woman who sees blood because of a wound.

steps.title: רבינא: Everyone holds וסתות are Rabbinic; the argument is about the מקור
steps.stepSummary: רבינא rejects the suggestion. Both may agree וסתות are דרבנן, and they argue about whether the place of the מקור is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: No. Everyone agrees וסתות are from the Rabbis. Here they argue about whether the place of the מקור is טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא pushes back on the suggested proof. He offers a different reason for the argument, so it does not have to be about וסתות at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof from step 19 only works if the argument has to be about וסתות. רבינא shows another way to read it: everyone holds וסתות are דרבנן, and the real question is whether blood that passes through the מקור becomes טמא, even wound blood.

keyTerms.meaning: its place is impure (it makes blood passing through it טמא)

phrases.english: Ravina said: No,
everyone holds וסתות are from the Rabbis,
and here they argue about whether the place of the source is impure.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the woman and the blood. The question here is not whether she is a נדה. It is whether the blood itself becomes טמא by passing through the מקור.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof suggested in step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof that רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל argue about וסתות.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The argument can be explained a different way, through the question of מקור מקומו טמא, so it does not prove anything about וסתות.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: The woman is pure, but the blood is impure
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: the woman is טהורה, but the blood is טמא because it came through the מקור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds: the woman is pure, but the blood is impure, because it came through the מקור.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא fills in his reading by explaining רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since וסתות are only דרבנן, we do not treat the woman as a נדה, so she is טהורה. But he holds the מקור's place is טמא, so the blood that passed through it, even wound blood, is טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: the woman is pure (she is not a נדה)
by way of the source (the uterus)

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel holds:
the woman is pure, but the blood is impure,
because it comes through the source.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how one side of the ברייתא fits רבינא's new reading.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Continues רבינא's rejection by explaining רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view without using the question of וסתות.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: His leniency for the woman comes from וסתות being דרבנן, which both sides agree to, not from the point they argue about.

steps.title: רבי's either-or argument against רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רבי argues that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's middle position does not hold up. Either the woman is טמאה too, or the blood is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said to him: If you worry that this is her period's blood, then the woman should be impure too. If you don't worry about her period, then the place of the מקור is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי challenges רבן שמעון בן גמליאל with an either-or argument. This shows what רבי holds in רבינא's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי holds the place of the מקור does not make blood טמא, so blood can only be טמא if it might really be נדה blood. If so, the woman is a נדה too. If not, the wound blood is טהור. So רבי rejects 'woman pure, blood impure' because he holds מקור מקומו טהור, not because of וסתות.

keyTerms.meaning: you are worried, you take into account

steps.whatToRemember: In רבינא's reading, both תנאים hold וסתות are דרבנן. They argue about whether the מקור makes blood טמא: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says yes, and רבי says no. So this ברייתא does not prove a dispute about וסתות.

phrases.english: And Rabbi said to him:
If you are concerned about her period,
then the woman is also impure,
and if you are not concerned about her period,
then the place of the source is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי: אִי חָיְישַׁתְּ לְוֶסֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי's answer to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, which finishes רבינא's reading of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling that the woman is טהורה but the blood is טמא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Either-or: if there is a worry about her period, she must be a נדה too. If there is no such worry, the blood is just wound blood, and the מקור's place does not make it טמא.

steps.title: בית שמאי: Two cloths for every act of intercourse
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה opens. בית שמאי rule that a woman needs two examination cloths for each act of תשמיש, or she must use a lamp.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: בית שמאי say: she needs two examination cloths for each and every act of intercourse, or she must have intercourse by the light of a lamp.
steps.whatsHappening: A brand-new משנה begins. בית שמאי give the first opinion on how often a woman must check herself during a night of תשמיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עד here is a cloth she uses to check for blood, once before and once after. בית שמאי want a fresh pair of checks around every act. The lamp option lets her look at the cloths right away instead of waiting until morning.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה, the base text the גמרא will discuss
Literally 'witnesses'; here, cloths used to check for blood
By the light of a lamp

steps.confusionAlert: עדים here does not mean people who testify. It means the checking cloths, which 'testify' whether there was blood or not.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Beit Shammai say:
She needs two examination cloths
phrases.notes: One check before and one check after.

phrases.english: for each and every act of intercourse,
or she must have intercourse by the light of a lamp.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the earlier discussion of רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: two checking cloths are needed for every act of תשמיש, or תשמיש must be done by lamplight.

steps.title: בית הלל: Two cloths for the whole night are enough
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל disagree. Two cloths cover the entire night: one before the first act and one after the last.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל say: it is enough for her to use two cloths for the whole night.
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל give the opposing opinion in the משנה. She does not need to check between each act, only at the start and end of the night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree she must check before and after. They disagree only about how often. בית שמאי require checks around every act, and בית הלל say one check at the beginning and one at the end of the whole night is enough.
steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי: two cloths for every act (or use a lamp). בית הלל: two cloths for the whole night.

phrases.english: Beit Hillel say:
it is enough for her with two cloths
for the whole night.
phrases.notes: One cloth before the first act and one after the last.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion to בית שמאי in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית הלל: two checking cloths cover the whole night.
